question: Does posing Koblitz index-calculus relation collection as an ordered search over a graph of canonicalised residual points — with an algebraic A* heuristic and small-norm Z[tau] multiplier edges — reduce forward node expansions per verified relation by >=2x over uniform-cost batched MITM at matched yield, and does the resulting arm beat the equal-envelope control (plain oracle on a base of size |F u D|) at all three section-5a price points, at the toy rungs n=31 and n=41 on K0 (the only rungs with a decomposition path: no n=131 path exists)? Separately, is cross-target forward-frontier sharing chance-level (preregistered NULL)?

claims.text: Cross-target forward-frontier sharing is chance-level. The measured fraction of forward node expansions saved by expanding one shared frontier for a batch of b=32 independent targets (vs b separate frontiers) is within [0.5x, 1.5x] of the birthday prediction f_share = b*E*n/r, i.e. f_share(n=31)~0.18 and f_share(n=41)~7.6e-4. There is NO structural overlap beyond chance.
claims.if_supported: The 'frontier sharing' that names this direction contributes ~0 at n=41 and nothing asymptotically (f_share -> 0 as r -> 2^129); the sharing sub-claim is closed and only the backward table T_d (already shared by batched MITM, not novel) is shared.
claims.if_not_supported: Sharing is real only if measured overlap > 1.5x prediction at n=41; that would be a surprise requiring an explanation of structural (non-birthday) cone overlap before any further spend.

claims.text: A*-on (order forward expansions by g+h, h = ONB-Hamming weight of x(rho) projected off the factor-base subspace) reduces forward node expansions per verified relation by >=2x versus uniform-cost (Dijkstra/BFS) MITM at matched verified-relation yield and matched backward table T_d, with CI-separated 95% bootstrap intervals, at n=31 and n=41.
claims.if_supported: The algebraic heuristic carries ordering signal; proceed to D1-BEAT to see whether the ordering gain survives the equal-envelope control.
claims.if_not_supported: The weight heuristic is too flat to order the search — consistent with SOLVER_SELECTION's no-routing-headroom finding on the same features. Combined with D1-SHARE supported, this triggers D1-COLLAPSE.

claims.text: The best D1 arm's GAE per verified relation AND cold end-to-end one-target GAE beat the equal-envelope control (plain per-target MITM on a base of size |F u D| at matched priced field-op budget) at ALL of 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per unpriced native operation (section-5a band).
claims.if_supported: D1 is a measured constant-factor improvement over the strongest matched control; report it as the distance remaining to matched rho (gap-to-rho), never as a pass. One rung, no exponent.
claims.if_not_supported: Any arm that wins at fixed columns but loses to the wider-base equal-envelope control at any price point is NOT an improvement — this is exactly how the double-large-prime graph was reduced to 2.1x. No priced row moves.

claims.text: Kill/collapse criterion: if D1-SHARE is supported (sharing null) AND D1-ASTAR is not supported (heuristic worthless), then all four 2x2 arms equal the existing batched-MITM + compact-orbit baseline within the A/A floor, and D1 reduces to a known method with nothing new claimed.
claims.if_supported: Verdict reduces_to_known: D1 == batched MITM + compact-orbit (already on main). The direction is closed; record it as a measured null so it is not reproposed.
claims.if_not_supported: At least one main effect is live; D1 stays open and D1-BEAT governs whether it is an improvement.

claims.text: Secondary/descriptive: the A* heuristic h is admissible on a fraction of peels measured as (1 - rate of peels with Delta-w > w_max), reported with a Wilson interval. Admissibility is NOT required for D1-ASTAR (which is about expansion count, not optimal-path guarantee); it is measured to characterise the search.
claims.if_supported: h is admissible; A* retains its optimal-path guarantee where it holds.
claims.if_not_supported: h is inadmissible on some peels; the search is weighted-A*/greedy/beam there, still valid, but without the optimal-path guarantee. No claim depends on admissibility.

claims.text: Out of scope: no complete-DLP sub-rho claim, no leaderboard or benchmarks/README.md row, no exponent or subexponential claim, and no n=131 / ECC2K-130 claim follow from this study. These are toy-rung (n<=41) relation-collection-phase cells with a matched one-target rho reported only as gap-to-rho. There is no decomposition path at n=131 (u64 FastPoint < n=64; MAX_MODULUS_BITS=63).

arms.description: Per-target frontier (sharing off), uniform-cost search (A* off) = the existing batched MITM pair-table (mitm-frobenius) + CADO filter. The primary baseline and the (sharing=off, heuristic=off) corner of the 2x2.

flags.heuristic: off (uniform cost / BFS over the same residual graph)
flags.oracle: mitm-frobenius (depth-1 forward layer + shared backward table T_d)
flags.multiplier_norm_N: matched across all candidate arms (frozen value TBD at freeze)
flags.factor_base: compact-orbit-scan (signed-Frobenius orbit reps; |F| frozen per cell)
flags.note: S0H0 is the only candidate arm whose behaviour already exists on main; it anchors the A/A floor and the matched baseline.

arms.description: Per-target frontier (sharing off), A* heuristic ON. Isolates the heuristic main effect.
Shared frontier (sharing ON), uniform cost (A* off). Isolates the sharing main effect; the n=31 cell of this arm is the cheap sharing-null test run FIRST.
Shared frontier (sharing ON), A* heuristic ON. The full hybrid; interaction cell.

THE DECISIVE CONTROL. Plain per-target MITM (sharing off, heuristic off) on a WIDER orbit-union base of size |F u D|, chosen so its total PRICED field-op budget matches the candidate arms' budget. This is the control that cut the double-large-prime graph from 23.8x to 2.1x; the candidate must beat THIS, not plain fixed-column IC.

parameters.base: orbit-union of size |F u D| at matched priced field-op budget

arms.description: Positive control: planted targets (target = a known sum of m factor-base reps). Every completed cell must recover a witness that re-adds in the curve group to the target. The planted scalar is NEVER solver input. Proves the instrument can find a relation that exists, per arm.

A/A: A-S0H0 re-run with a second derived seed, identical arguments otherwise. Counted outcomes (expansions, relations, columns) compared as the noise floor; any effect below the A/A spread is not reported.

Matched reference: rho.signed_frobenius on the SAME target, SAME process, SAME counted unit (GAE), run cold, unpriced work priced the same way across the section-5a band. Reported ONLY as gap-to-rho (best arm GAE / matched-rho GAE) as the distance remaining, never as a pass/fail gate. At these rungs IC sits ~17x rho after the large-prime round.

parameters.cheapest_config: the cheapest registered rho variant on the same instance/targets across the band (plain, negation, signed-Frobenius-fold; with/without setup variants)

factors.name: factor base |F| and multiplier norm N
factors.how: Frozen per cell; identical across the 2x2 and the A/A; the equal-envelope control's wider base |F u D| is sized to match the candidate priced field-op budget, which is the whole point of the control.

factors.name: backward table depth d (T_d)
factors.how: Same d on every candidate arm; T_d is target-independent and shared even by the baseline, so its sharing is not credited to D1.

factors.name: batch size b
factors.how: 32 independent public targets per seed; sharing is measured as forward-expansion overlap across this batch.

factors.name: counted instrument
factors.how: ONE example binary (transport_graph_cell) counts GAE identically on every arm including the equal-envelope control and the matched rho; sha256 pins it at freeze.

factors.name: host class and threads
factors.how: One single-threaded process per cell; host facts recorded per row; timing is diagnostic only (the ranked unit is counted GAE).

factors.name: arm order
factors.how: The four 2x2 arms and the equal-envelope control are interleaved within a cell, not blocked, so drift cannot align with an arm.

factors.name: analyst / labels
factors.how: Arm labels are MASKED during analysis; the export is frozen before unmasking (see randomization.blinding).

factors.name: spot preemption
factors.how: Worker/node/interruption recorded per row; an interrupted cell is discarded and re-run whole on an admitted worker (counted units survive; wall time is invalid after restore).

factors.name: unpriced native ops
factors.how: canonicalisation, hash probes, heuristic evaluation, matroid-greedy steps counted as named native counters and swept at 0 / 0.1 / 1 GAE each (section-5a); ranking holds only where the order holds across the band.

comparisons.reason: Measured forward-expansion overlap fraction across the b=32 batch vs the birthday prediction f_share = b*E*n/r. Decides D1-SHARE. The n=31 cell is where overlap is largest (~0.18) and is run first.
Forward node expansions per verified relation, A*-on vs uniform cost, at matched yield and matched T_d; 95% bootstrap CI. Decides D1-ASTAR; admissibility rate reported (D1-ADMISSIBLE).

Best candidate arm's GAE/relation and cold end-to-end one-target GAE vs the equal-envelope control at 0/0.1/1 GAE. Decides D1-BEAT. The ranked verdict holds only if it holds at all three price points.
Noise floor; counted outcomes must agree within the A/A spread.
Main effects (sharing, heuristic) and their interaction; D1-COLLAPSE fires if both main effects are null within the A/A floor.
Gap-to-rho = best-arm GAE / matched-rho GAE across the band; reported as distance remaining, never pass/fail.

randomization.arm_order_reason: Within a cell the four 2x2 arms and the equal-envelope control run interleaved per target so host drift and preemption cannot align with one arm. Cell order runs n=31 before n=41 so the cheap sharing-null cell (n=31) resolves D1-SHARE before any n=41 spend.

power.note: D1-ASTAR needs a 2x expansion-ratio with a CI excluding 1.0; 32 targets x 6 seeds = 192 verified-relation samples per arm per cell gives a tight paired bootstrap at the toy rungs. Power is re-checked on the n=31 cell before committing the n=41 spend. Exact instance counts are frozen here; the stopping rule can only lower the n=41 spend.

primary.name: Forward node expansions per verified relation
primary.definition: Number of forward residual-node expansions divided by verified relations, per arm per cell. The core quantity for D1-ASTAR; independent of isolation.

primary.name: Cross-target forward-expansion overlap fraction
primary.definition: Fraction of forward expansions in the shared-frontier arm that serve >=2 of the b=32 targets, i.e. saved vs b separate frontiers. Compared to f_share = b*E*n/r. Decides D1-SHARE.

primary.name: GAE per verified relation
primary.definition: Total priced GAE / verified relations, read across the section-5a band (0, 0.1, 1 GAE per unpriced native op). For D1-BEAT.

primary.name: Cold one-target end-to-end GAE
primary.definition: From instance to a verified [k]P=Q for one public target, all target-independent setup charged in full (SUCCESS_CRITERIA section 1), across the band. The headline cost for the gap-to-rho and for D1-BEAT.

secondary.name: A* heuristic admissibility rate
secondary.definition: 1 - (fraction of peels with Delta-w > w_max); w_max measured, not assumed. Wilson interval. Decides D1-ADMISSIBLE (descriptive).

secondary.name: Unpriced native operation counts
secondary.definition: canonicalisation, hash probes, heuristic evaluations, matroid-greedy steps; the inputs to the section-5a band sweep.

secondary.name: Gap to matched rho
secondary.definition: best-arm end_to_end_one_target_gae / matched rho.signed_frobenius GAE, per band point. Distance remaining, never a pass/fail.

secondary.name: Process wall seconds
secondary.definition: Diagnostic only; the ranked unit is counted GAE. Valid only on native-L2 admission; invalid after a CRIU restore.

stopping_rules.rule: Phase 0 (cheap gate): run the n=31 cells of A-S1H0 vs A-S0H0 (and the A/A) FIRST. If the measured sharing_overlap_fraction is within [0.5x,1.5x] of f_share(n=31)~0.18 (D1-SHARE supported), the sharing sub-claim is closed; the shared-frontier arms at n=41 are still run only to confirm f_share~7.6e-4, not to find a win.

Phase 1 gate on the n=41 spend: only commit the full n=41 2x2 + equal-envelope spend if the n=31 A*-on arm (C-astar-expansions) shows a point estimate >=2x forward-expansion cut. If the n=31 A* effect is below the A/A floor, record D1-ASTAR not_supported at n=31 and do NOT spend on n=41 candidate arms (run only the n=41 baseline + rho reference for the gap record).
Fixed grid otherwise: 2 curves x 2 m x {4 candidate arms + equal-envelope + positive + A/A} + matched rho, 32 targets x 6 seeds per cell; interleaved; seeds derived from the frozen root seed.

Invalidation stop: a failed positive control (a completed planted cell with no verified witness), a binary sha256 different from the frozen one, or a worker without native-L2 admission for a timed row stops the affected shard for the director's assessment; no threshold is changed.

invalidation_rules: A completed planted (positive-control) cell whose witness does not re-add in the curve group to the target invalidates that (arm, cell).
A candidate cell whose verified_relations differs from its claimed relations (a witness that does not re-add) is invalid.
An A/A pair whose counted outcomes differ beyond the recorded noise floor invalidates both and halts the shard.
A binary whose sha256 differs from the frozen value, or a source tree off the frozen commit, makes the row's timing diagnostic only; counted GAE from a wrong binary is invalid.
Reading wall seconds from a run without native-L2 admission as timing evidence is inadmissible (counted GAE is still the ranked unit).

decision_rule.text: D1-SHARE supported iff measured sharing_overlap_fraction is within [0.5x,1.5x] of b*E*n/r at both rungs. D1-ASTAR supported iff A*-on forward-expansions/relation <= 0.5x A*-off at matched yield with a CI excluding 1.0, at n=31 and n=41. D1-BEAT supported iff the best candidate arm's gae_per_relation AND end_to_end_one_target_gae beat C-equal-envelope at ALL of 0/0.1/1 GAE. D1-COLLAPSE fires (verdict reduces_to_known) iff D1-SHARE supported AND D1-ASTAR not supported and the 2x2 arms equal A-S0H0 within the A/A floor. Every reported ratio is accompanied by gap-to-rho as the distance remaining; nothing here is a pass/fail against rho.
decision_rule.threshold: Sharing: [0.5x,1.5x] of f_share. A*: <=0.5x expansions at matched yield, CI excludes 1.0. Beat: strictly cheaper than equal-envelope at all three band points. Collapse: within A/A floor.
decision_rule.statistic: Paired bootstrap (95%) on forward-expansions/relation and GAE; per-cell overlap fraction vs birthday prediction; band-wise GAE ratios.
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: forward-expansion ratio (A*-off / A*-on); GAE ratio (best arm / equal-envelope) per band point; gap-to-rho.

Running any candidate arm before the instrument sha256 is frozen and its preflight is recorded.
Reporting the sharing arm as a win if the overlap matches the birthday prediction (D1-SHARE is a preregistered null).
Claiming an improvement from an arm that beats fixed-column IC but loses to the equal-envelope control at any band point.
Using wall seconds from a non-L2 run, or the preflight, as evidence.
Presenting these toy-rung relation-collection cells as a complete-DLP result, a sub-rho claim, a leaderboard row, or any n=131/ECC2K-130 statement (D1-OOS).
Dropping the gap-to-rho from any reported ratio.

literature.claim: Full D1 design: graph formulation, A* heuristic, the computed sharing null f_share=b*E*n/r, novelty vs large-prime graph / MITM / compact-orbit-scan.
The equal-envelope control reduced the double-large-prime graph from 23.8x to 2.1x; the candidate must beat the wider-base control, not fixed-column IC.

The ONB x-weight / Frobenius-distance features (the A* heuristic candidate) gave the learned selector NO routing headroom on 288 queries. Preregistered as the main risk that the heuristic is too flat.
A residual-collision walk (nodes=residuals, edges=subtract base point, MITM meet) already exists and costs ~1 rho solve per relation; D1's increment over it is the ordering (A*) and multiplier edges.
Small-norm Z[tau] multiplier edges exist as a base-enlargement move (measured 9.2x one-target total vs plain-scan at n=41,m=3); D1 reuses them as search edges.
u64 FastPoint path stops at n<64; koblitz_sparse_la MAX_MODULUS_BITS=63; no decomposition search runs at n=131. The protocol tops out at n<=41.
